paper.title: The observed-data likelihood of ADAM and iETS with unobserved periods

definitions.definition: State space form of a time series model, also called the innovations form, in which the observation equation and the state transition share one error term $\epsilon_t$ per period: $$\begin{aligned} z_t &= w(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l}) + r(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l})\epsilon_t \\ \mathbf v_t &= f(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l}) + g(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l})\epsilon_t. \end{aligned}$$

A period $t$ at which the potential value $z_t$ of the modelled variable is not observed ($O_t=0$): a period with zero demand in an intermittent demand model, where the demand size is not observed, or a period with a missing value.

The joint density of the observed data only, obtained by integrating the complete-data likelihood over the values $\mathbf z_{\mathrm{mis}}$ at the unobserved periods: $$L(\theta)=\int f(\mathbf y_{\mathrm{obs}},\mathbf z_{\mathrm{mis}};\theta)\,d\mathbf z_{\mathrm{mis}}.$$

The objective of the iETS estimator of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023, eq. B.6): the sum of the one-step log-densities of the observed demand sizes, minus the differential entropy $H_z(\hat\mu_t,\sigma)$ of the size at each period with zero demand, plus the Bernoulli log-likelihood of the occurrence.

The estimator used in ADAM and in iETS (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, Appendix C): the single source of error recursion run with $\epsilon_t=0$ at the unobserved periods and with the fixed persistence vector $\mathbf g$ at the observed ones, with the likelihood taken as the product of one-step densities at the observed periods.

Pure multiplicative exponential smoothing in the form of the Augmented Dynamic Adaptive Model, in which each component $k$ is updated by the factor $(1+\epsilon_t)^{g_k}$; for ETS(M,Md,M) with seasonal period $m$, $$\begin{aligned} z_t &= l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}s_{t-m}(1+\epsilon_t) \\ l_t &= l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\epsilon_t)^{\alpha} \\ b_t &= b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\epsilon_t)^{\beta} \\ s_t &= s_{t-m}(1+\epsilon_t)^{\gamma}. \end{aligned}$$

Pure multiplicative exponential smoothing in the form of Hyndman et al. (2008), in which each component $k$ is updated by the factor $1+g_k\epsilon_t$; for ETS(M,Md,M) with seasonal period $m$, $$\begin{aligned} z_t &= l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}s_{t-m}(1+\epsilon_t) \\ l_t &= l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\alpha\epsilon_t) \\ b_t &= b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\beta\epsilon_t) \\ s_t &= s_{t-m}(1+\gamma\epsilon_t). \end{aligned}$$

The recursion for the conditional mean $\mathbf a_t$ and scaled covariance $\mathbf P_t$ of the state of a linear single source of error model: at an observed period $$\begin{aligned} v_t &= z_t-\mathbf w'\mathbf a_t \\ f_t &= \mathbf w'\mathbf P_t\mathbf w+1 \\ \mathbf k_t &= (\mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf w+\mathbf g)/f_t \\ \mathbf a_{t+1} &= \mathbf F\mathbf a_t+\mathbf k_t v_t \\ \mathbf P_{t+1} &= \mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf F'+\mathbf g\mathbf g'-\mathbf k_t\mathbf k_t'f_t; \end{aligned}$$ at an unobserved period $$\begin{aligned} \mathbf a_{t+1} &= \mathbf F\mathbf a_t \\ \mathbf P_{t+1} &= \mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf F'+\mathbf g\mathbf g'; \end{aligned}$$ started from $\mathbf a_1=\mathbf x_0$, $\mathbf P_1=\mathbf 0$.

The change $d_t=\log(\mu_t/\hat\mu_t)$ of the logarithm of the location of a pure multiplicative model accumulated over the unobserved periods since the last observed period, relative to the point forecast $\hat\mu_t$ with zero errors.

Approximate predictive density of a demand size after $j_t-1$ unobserved periods: the one-step density $f_z(z_t\mid\hat\mu_t e^{d})$ mixed over a normal [[D9:drift of the states]] $d\sim\mathcal N(m_t,w_t)$, with $m_t$, $w_t$ computed by 32-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature on the quantile function of $1+\epsilon$ and the mixture by Gauss-Hermite quadrature.
The density of a demand size after an interval taken as the one-step density $f_z(z_t\mid\hat\mu_t)$ of the model, without the [[D9:drift of the states]] over the unobserved periods.

Intermittent demand sizes $$z_t=l_{t-1}(1+\epsilon_t)$$ with $\E(1+\epsilon_t)=1$ and $\Var(1+\epsilon_t)=s$, Gamma, log-normal or inverse Gaussian $1+\epsilon_t$ (the greybox parameterisation of the package) and the level moving at every period, observed or not: $$l_t=l_{t-1}(1+\epsilon_t)^\alpha$$ in the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] and $$l_t=l_{t-1}(1+\alpha\epsilon_t)$$ in the [[D7:conventional multiplicative ETS]].

The exact density of the size after an interval, computed on a grid of step 0.001 in $\log z$ by FFT convolution with tails cut at 1e-12, compared with an approximation by the largest Kullback-Leibler divergence per observation over $s$ from 0.05 to 1 in steps of 0.05, $\alpha$ from 0.1 to 0.6 in steps of 0.05 and $j$ from 2 to 20 (kl_mixture.py); a refinement of 164 cells halved the step and cut the tails at 1e-14.
The divergence $\int g\log(g/h)$ of an approximate density $h$ from the exact density $g$, per observation; over a grid, its largest value.

The estimator of the scale $s$ of Gamma or inverse Gaussian sizes that solves the moment equation $s=h(s)$, built from the moments of the drift factor $D_t$, by the iteration $s\leftarrow h(s)$ from the one-step estimate, stopping at $|s_{new}-s|\le 10^{-10}s$ or after 100 iterations; a fit fails when an iterate is not positive and finite, the iteration does not converge, or the value leaves the admissible range.

definitions.term: Monte Carlo study of the scale
definitions.definition: 480 cells of relative errors simulated with the drift ($s\in\{0.05,0.2,0.5,1\}$, $\alpha\in\{0.1,0.3,0.6\}$, intervals fixed at 2, 5 or 10 or geometric with occurrence probability 0.5 or 0.2, 100 or 1000 observed sizes) and 120 cells within fitted models ($s\in\{0.05,0.5\}$, 100 observed sizes), 2000 replications per cell from numpy SeedSequence(20261015) with one child stream per cell; cells grouped by the drift order $\E(j-1)\alpha^2s$ (scale_recovery.py).
The relative bias of a scale estimate, (mean estimate $- s$)$/s$ over the replications of a cell; its median over cells.
The share of replications in which the scale estimator fails.

The prediction interval of pure multiplicative ETS in the smooth package (generate_prediction_interval with var_anal): the point forecast with zero errors times the quantile of the distribution with mean one and variance $$V_h=(1+v)(1+\alpha^2v)^{h-1}-1,$$ $v=\Var(1+\epsilon)$; for the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] with the log-normal distribution, exact in logarithms.

ETS(M,N,N) with $s=0.32$, $\alpha=0.21$, 100 observations and initial level 10, with Gamma, inverse Gaussian or log-normal errors, in the ADAM and conventional forms; in the second case the last six of the 100 periods unobserved.

The 0.95 quantile of 1,000,000 simulated paths divided by the point forecast with zero errors, twelve steps ahead and 18 steps from the last observed period after six unobserved periods at the end of the sample (interval_bounds.py, seed 20261015).

definitions.term: upper bound over the point forecast
definitions.definition: The upper bound of the 90% prediction interval (its 0.95 quantile) divided by the point forecast with zero errors.

The [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] with the scaled state covariance kept as a low-rank factor $\mathbf P_t=\mathbf U_t\mathbf U_t'$, updated by rank one at each observed period, as in the C++ core of smooth (src/headers/adamCore.h).
The [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] with the whole scaled state covariance matrix $\mathbf P_t$.

1344 hourly observations, generated by ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with lags 24 and 168 or following a fixed sine pattern, with 1 to 48 nested missing values, fitted by ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with lags 24 and 168 (193 state cells), the normal distribution and backcast initial states.

25 interleaved repetitions per case of the fits with the two forms of the filter, both built from smooth commit 53104ee9, on one cloud VM (Intel Xeon 2.80 GHz, 4 vCPUs, Linux 6.18.44, Python 3.11.15) with one thread (lowrank_timing.py).
The median run time of the [[D24:full covariance form]] divided by that of the [[D23:low-rank factor form]].

The approximation of the predictive density of a pure additive model with Laplace, S or Generalised Normal errors that keeps the error in its family with scale $sf_t^{1/p}$, $p$ such that the variance is proportional to $s^p$, as in the smooth package.
The mixture of the error density over the normal uncertainty of the states by a Gauss-Hermite rule with $Q$ nodes (16 in the smooth package).
Laplace, S and Generalised Normal (shape 0.5 to 3) errors with scale $s=1$, convolved with normal state uncertainty of variance $(f_t-1)V(s)$, for 22 values of $f_t$ from 1.01 to 100 (kl_laplace.py).
The Kullback-Leibler divergence in both directions between the exact convolution and each approximation, by composite 8-node Gauss-Legendre integration (kl_laplace.py).
For a size with density $f_z$, $$H_z = -\E\log f_z = -\int f_z(z)\log f_z(z)\,dz.$$

claims.statement: The errors $\epsilon_t$ of the single source of error model are independent across periods.
In the intermittent demand model the occurrence $o_t$ is independent of the potential demand size $z_t$.
The potential demand size $z_t$ has a continuous distribution, so that $P(z_t=0)=0$.
Whether a period is observed carries no information about the unobserved value $z_t$ beyond the model, so that the missing values are missing at random.
The initial states of the single source of error model are fixed parameters, so that the state covariance is zero at the start of the sample.
The errors of the pure additive model are normally distributed with constant variance $\sigma^2$.
In the log-normal ADAM multiplicative ETS, $\log(1+\epsilon_t)\sim\mathcal N(-s/2,s)$, so that $\E(1+\epsilon_t)=1$.
The [[D9:drift of the states]] of a pure multiplicative model over an interval is approximately normally distributed, with the states known at the previous observed period.

warrants.text: With a dynamic scale model, the scale at each period with zero demand is a free function of the parameters and enters the entropy-augmented likelihood only through the term $-H_z$; for the normal distribution $-H_z=-\frac12\log(2\pi e\sigma^2)$ increases without bound as $\sigma\to0$, and for the Gamma distribution the entropy decreases in the scale for large values, so the objective has no finite maximum.

The SSOE Kalman filter coincides with the single source of error recursion whenever its covariance is zero; the covariance starts at zero after backcasting and becomes non-zero only at an unobserved period, so on series without unobserved periods the last forward pass performs the same operations as the recursion.

limitations.statement: Within a model fitted by the zero-error recursion, the fixed-point moment estimate of the Gamma and inverse Gaussian scale is biased upwards, because the states after an interval are updated with gain $\mathbf g$ and part of the drift leaks into the following errors.
The low-rank timing comparison uses one model configuration and one series length on one cloud VM (Intel Xeon 2.80 GHz, 4 vCPUs).
